zeitlin2013.citation: Zeitlin C. et al. Measurements of energetic particle radiation in transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory. Science 340:1080-1084 (2013).
zeitlin2013.evidence: Measured. One instrument (MSL RAD) inside the cruise stage, 253 days.

hassler2014.citation: Hassler D.M. et al. Mars' surface radiation environment measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity rover. Science 343:1244797 (2014).
hassler2014.evidence: Measured on the surface, one instrument (RAD). The full-mission value is a model estimate.

std3001.short: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C, via OCHMO-TB-020 Rev G
std3001.citation: NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, Volume 1: Crew Health, Rev C. Requirements [V1 4029] ALARA, [V1 4030] career limit 600 mSv, [V1 4031] SPE limit 250 mSv. As quoted in NASA OCHMO Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020 Rev G, Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection (6 June 2025).
std3001.evidence: NASA standard. The 600 mSv career limit is set from a 3% mean risk of cancer death. The 250 mSv SPE limit is a design requirement for the reference event (sum of the October 1989 events).

std3001appF.citation: NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, Volume 2: Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health, Appendix F (display and alert classes).

noaaScale.citation: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center. Space Weather Scales: Solar Radiation Storms (S1 = 10 pfu of protons at 10 MeV or more).
noaaScale.evidence: Operational definition. Check against the DONKI SEP definition before the pitch.

donki.citation: NASA CCMC Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI): FLR, CME, and SEP records.
donki.evidence: Event catalog near Earth. It does not measure dose at the vehicle.

george2024.citation: George S.P., Gaza R., Matthiä D., ... Berger T. et al. Space radiation measurements during the Artemis I lunar mission. Nature 634:48-52 (2024).
george2024.evidence: Measured on Orion, Artemis I (2022), uncrewed, 1 flight. In the inner proton belt (a proxy for a large SPE), the storm shelter read 134 µGy/min and the crew cabin read 287 µGy/min (ratio 0.47). A model of the October 1989 SPE gives 95 and 414 µGy/min (ratio 0.23). Orion keeps a large SPE to 150 mSv or less in the shelter.

team.citation: CSI team value for the Space Apps 2026 demo. Not a NASA flight rule. See PRD CSI-HM-PRD-001 Rev D, section 07.

lee2020sans.citation: Lee A.G. et al. Spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS) and the neuro-ophthalmologic effects of microgravity: a review and an update. npj Microgravity 6:7 (2020).
lee2020sans.evidence: Review. Changes in near vision are a common first sign. Diagnosis needs an eye exam.

law2014co2.citation: Law J. et al. Relationship between carbon dioxide levels and reported headaches on the International Space Station. J Occup Environ Med 56(5):477-483 (2014).
law2014co2.evidence: Observational, ISS crews. Headache odds rise with cabin CO2.

leblanc2000bone.short: LeBlanc et al., J Musculoskelet Neuronal Interact 2000
leblanc2000bone.citation: LeBlanc A. et al. Bone mineral and lean tissue loss after long duration space flight. J Musculoskelet Neuronal Interact 1(2):157-160 (2000).
leblanc2000bone.evidence: Measured, Mir crews. Hip bone loss of about 1 to 1.6% per month.

barger2014sleep.citation: Barger L.K. et al. Prevalence of sleep deficiency and use of hypnotic drugs in astronauts before, during, and after spaceflight. Lancet Neurol 13(9):904-912 (2014).
barger2014sleep.evidence: Observational, actigraphy. Mean sleep in flight was 5.96 h a night on the shuttle and 6.09 h on the ISS.

hrpBmed.citation: NASA Human Research Program. Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Conditions and Psychiatric Disorders. Evidence report.
hrpBmed.evidence: Evidence report. Mood and sleep trends are early signs. Thresholds here are team values.

iaeaArs.citation: IAEA. Medical Management of Radiation Injuries. Safety Reports Series No. 101 (2020). Prodromal signs of acute radiation syndrome.
iaeaArs.evidence: Clinical guidance. Nausea and vomiting are prodromal signs at doses far above the doses in this demo.

hrpCardio.citation: NASA Human Research Program. Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes. Evidence report.
hrpCardio.evidence: Evidence report. Heart rate limits here are team values for the demo.

rad2012.citation: MSL RAD team. MSL RAD Reduced Data Records, data set MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0. NASA Planetary Data System, PPI node.
rad2012.evidence: Measured. RAD E detector (plastic, near tissue) in the MSL cruise stage, 5 to 11 March 2012. Our parse gives a cruise background of 443.1 µGy/day, the same as Löwe et al. 2025.

lowe2025.citation: Löwe et al. 2025. arXiv:2502.02469. Onboard alarm for solar particle events from MSL RAD dose rates.
lowe2025.evidence: Preprint with a method tested on RAD data. Background: linear fit to the previous 5 days.

phase4.citation: Vigil team. Phase 4 real-data test of shelter rules on MSL RAD events. research/realdata/RESULTS.md in this repository.
phase4.evidence: Measured data, 7 events, 541 days scored. Tuned on cycle 24 events, tested once on cycle 25 events. Small sample.

goesFlares.short: NOAA GOES X-ray flare list and CDAW CME catalog
goesFlares.citation: NOAA NCEI GOES XRS event reports (2012). SOHO LASCO CME Catalog, CDAW Data Center, NASA GSFC.
goesFlares.evidence: Measured. Used for the replay records because the DONKI host refused connections from our test system.

ochmoCo2.citation: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer. Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004, Carbon Dioxide (2023). Cites NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004] and Law et al., J Occup Environ Med 2014.
ochmoCo2.evidence: NASA standard. The 2.5 mmHg weekly value comes from a retrospective study of 49 ISS crew (Law et al. 2014).

ochmoEclss.citation: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer. Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-002, Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (2023). Cites NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6003, 6006, 6012, 6013].
ochmoEclss.evidence: NASA standard. The brief says to confirm values against NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev D.

nasem2021.citation: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. Space Radiation and Astronaut Health: Managing and Communicating Cancer Risks. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press (2021). Table 3-1.
nasem2021.evidence: Consensus report. ESA, CSA, and the Russian agency set a career limit of 1,000 mSv effective dose for all ages and sexes. JAXA uses a 3% cancer-death risk (500 to 1,000 mSv).
